card.name: Linking words in old-style prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as for, to, of, in and on that come right after a noun or verb in older, formal English prose, often before an abstract noun or verb.

modes.label: Preposition after a noun
modes.description: A word like for, of or to follows an abstract noun such as movement, favor or powers.
modes.example: a comprehensive argument in favor<< of>> the conservation of the state's forest resources

modes.label: Preposition or to after a verb
modes.description: The word to or in follows a verb or participle, and a gerund or action comes next.

modes.label: Linking verb or in
modes.description: A short word such as is or in follows a subject in a scholarly explanation.
modes.example: This rhythmicity<< is>> probably inherent in the heart muscle

card.plain: It fires on small linking words in old-fashioned essay or biography prose, just before the idea they introduce.
